It changes only two test files, and no product code.\n\n- `tests/e2e/multiselect-aria.test.ts` has two new tests. `issue label picker exposes its combobox state` drives the picker from the keyboard and checks its `role`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls` and `aria-activedescendant`, and checks where focus goes after Escape. `issue label picker reports collapsed after Escape` records bug #104 with `test.fail()`.\n- The three label picker tests now share a `withLabeledIssue` helper for setup and cleanup. The existing test kept its steps and comments. Only its indentation changed.\n- `tests/e2e/menus.test.ts` has a new test, `navbar menu triggers name their menus`. It checks every `<aria-menu>` trigger in the navbar for `aria-haspopup=\"menu\"` and for an `aria-controls` that names a `role=\"menu\"` element. A failure names the trigger.\n\n## Why\n\nA later change to `web_src/js/modules/fomantic/dropdown.ts` or to `<aria-menu>` could remove these attributes without breaking any existing test. These checks fail when that happens, and the failure names the attribute.\n\n- **AC1.** The picker is a `combobox`. Its `aria-expanded` is `false` before focus and `true` after. Its `aria-controls` equals the menu's `id`.\n- **AC2.** After ArrowDown, `aria-activedescendant` names an element with `role=\"option\"` inside that menu.\n- **AC3.** After Escape, the list is hidden and focus stays on the picker. The `aria-expanded=\"false\"` check fails on `main`, so it is the separate `test.fail()` test (AC6).\n- **AC4.** The navbar test covers every `<aria-menu>` trigger instead of a fixed list of names.\n- **AC5.** Every new or changed test calls `assertNoJsError`. Each one finishes in under 2 s locally.\n- **AC6.** Every check passes on `main` except the Escape check, which links #104.\n\n## How it was tested\n\nThe new checks extend the two existing test files, as Decision 2 in #65 says.\n\nThe new label picker checks are a separate test instead of more steps in the existing one. A label change makes `reloadPagePartially()` replace the whole sidebar, which drops focus, so the existing flow cannot check focus after Escape.\n\nThe Escape bug only shows when the user waits before pressing Escape. Focusing the picker schedules an ARIA refresh 100 ms later, and that refresh sets `aria-expanded` to `false` when Escape came first. The `test.fail()` test installs Playwright's fake clock and advances it 200 ms before Escape, so the refresh has already run. The test advances a fake clock. It does not sleep.\n\n## CI / manual verification\n\n```sh\nGITEA_TEST_E2E_FLAGS='tests/e2e/multiselect-aria.test.ts tests/e2e/menus.test.ts --project=chromium --project=webkit --reporter=list' make test-e2e\n```\n\n- 19 tests passed, and 1 was skipped. The skipped test is the existing WebKit Tab test.\n- The new tests took between 0.3 s and 1.5 s each, in Chromium and in WebKit.\n- With its `test.fail()` line removed, the Escape test failed in both browsers on the intended assertion, with `Expected: \"false\"` and `Received: \"true\"`.\n- Firefox was not run locally because it hangs at launch on macOS 27. CI runs it.\n- `pnpm exec eslint --max-warnings=0` passes on both files.\n\n`./.claude-students/check.sh` reports two docs over their line caps, `docs/models-issues.md` and `guide/models-issues.md`. This PR does not change either file, and `main` has the same report.\n\n## Design\n\nThis PR follows Decision 1 (assert ARIA state in Playwright) and Decision 2 (extend the label picker test and the navbar test) in #65. The `withLabeledIssue` helper and the separate tests are not in the issue. The previous section explains why they are needed.\n\n## Tech Debt\n\n**Introduced:** The label picker selectors depend on Fomantic's dropdown markup (`.ui.dropdown`, `> .menu`). A comment on the shared locator says to update them if #25 moves the picker off Fomantic. The Escape test also depends on the 100 ms refresh delay in `dropdown.ts`. If that delay becomes longer than 200 ms, the test must advance the clock further.\n\n**Encountered:** `dropdown.ts` does not refresh `aria-expanded` when Escape closes the list. I filed #104 and recorded it with `test.fail()` instead of fixing it here, because #65 puts fixes out of scope. The repo topics test in the same file takes about 2.5 s, which is over the 2 s target. This PR does not change that test.\n\n## AI assistance\n\nClaude Code (claude-opus-5-5) wrote the tests, ran them, and found that the Escape bug only appears after a wait. It also drafted #104 and this description. I reviewed the diff, re-ran the suite and the unmarked failing test, and can explain each assertion. ---
name: review-dont-fix-student-prs
description: "On student PRs: report findings, never offer to apply the fixes"
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

When reviewing a student's PR, hand back the findings and stop. Do not offer to reword the commit,
add the missing trailer, or apply the cleanups — the student makes each change themselves, one
change per commit.

**Why:** CSCI435 coursework. Landing several concerns in one commit is the habit being corrected;
a commit that does one thing would have exposed its own missing details at review time. Fixing it
for them removes both lessons. Same principle as [[teach-through-navigation]].

**How to apply:** name each finding with its `file:line` and say which rule or neighbouring code it
conflicts with, so the student can act on it unaided. Verify with the repo's own tooling
(see [[prefers-make-targets]]) and report what passed. End the review at the findings — no "want me
to stage it?".
---
name: lean-review-workflows
description: "Review workflows must be lean (about 3 agents, ~230k tokens); never the full multi-agent review"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: f882d2ed-5eb7-4bc9-91b7-649494d2641e
  modified: 2026-10-19T23:00:57.608Z
---

When the user asks for a review workflow, run a small one: two scoped reviewers in parallel plus a
single skeptic that verifies all findings together, each capped at ~5 findings, no servers, e2e or
full lint runs inside the agents. On #58 (2026-10-19) that cost ~232k tokens and found 2 real
issues. The full review on #56 (13 agents) cost ~856k.

**Why:** "Please, please, please, do not do a full review workflow, as that will absolutely chew
through my session limit" (2026-10-19). Session limits are the constraint.

**How to apply:** state the agent count and a token estimate before launching. Also check how the
course's real reviewers behave (teammate's AI-assisted rubric + CodeRabbit pre-merge checks in
`.coderabbit.yaml`) and flag surface-level things they'd catch; the user often answers those with
a manual pushback instead of a change (screenshots check, combined "What changed and why" heading,
attribute-only e2e checks). Related: [[sim-58-59-dry-run]], [[one-step-at-a-time]].

function attachDomEvents(dropdown: HTMLElement, focusable: HTMLElement, menu: HTMLElement) {
  // when showing, it has class: ".animating.in"
  // when hiding, it has class: ".visible.animating.out"
  const isMenuVisible = () => (menu.classList.contains('visible') && !menu.classList.contains('out')) || menu.classList.contains('in');

  // update aria attributes according to current active/selected item
  const refreshAriaActiveItem = () => {
    const menuVisible = isMenuVisible();
    focusable.setAttribute('aria-expanded', menuVisible ? 'true' : 'false');

    // if there is an active item, use it (the user is navigating between items)
    // otherwise use the "selected" for combobox (for the last selected item)
    const active = $(menu).find('> .item.active, > .item.selected, > .scrolling.menu > .item.selected')[0];
    if (!active) return;
    // if the popup is visible and has an active/selected item, use its id as aria-activedescendant
    if (menuVisible) {
      focusable.setAttribute('aria-activedescendant', active.id);
    } else if ((dropdown as any)[ariaPatchKey].listPopupRole === 'menu') {
      // for menu, when the popup is hidden, no need to keep the aria-activedescendant, and clear the active/selected item
      focusable.removeAttribute('aria-activedescendant');
      active.classList.remove('active', 'selected');
    }
  };

  dropdown.addEventListener('keydown', (e: KeyboardEvent) => {
    if (e.isComposing) return;
    // here it must use keydown event before dropdown's keyup handler, otherwise there is no Enter event in our keyup handler
    if (e.key === 'Enter') {
      const elItem = menu.querySelector<HTMLElement>(':scope > .item.selected, .menu > .item.selected');
      // if the selected item is clickable, then trigger the click event.
      // we can not click any item without check, because Fomantic code might also handle the Enter event. that would result in double click.
      if (elItem?.matches('a, .js-aria-clickable') && !elItem.matches('.tw-hidden, .filtered')) {
        e.preventDefault();
        elItem.click();
      }
    }
  });

  // use setTimeout to run the refreshAria in next tick (to make sure the Fomantic UI code has finished its work)
  // do not return any value, jQuery has return-value related behaviors.
  // when the popup is hiding, it's better to have a small "delay", because there is a Fomantic UI animation
  // without the delay for hiding, the UI will be somewhat laggy and sometimes may get stuck in the animation.
  const deferredRefreshAriaActiveItem = (delay = 0) => { setTimeout(refreshAriaActiveItem, delay) };
  (dropdown as any)[ariaPatchKey].deferredRefreshAriaActiveItem = deferredRefreshAriaActiveItem;
  dropdown.addEventListener('keyup', (e) => { if (e.key.startsWith('Arrow')) deferredRefreshAriaActiveItem(); });

  // if the dropdown has been opened by focus, do not trigger the next click event again.
  // otherwise the dropdown will be closed immediately, especially on Android with TalkBack
  // * desktop event sequence: mousedown -> focus -> mouseup -> click
  // * mobile event sequence: focus -> mousedown -> mouseup -> click
  // Fomantic may stop propagation of blur event, use capture to make sure we can still get the event
  let ignoreClickPreEvents = 0, ignoreClickPreVisible = 0;
  dropdown.addEventListener('mousedown', () => {
    ignoreClickPreVisible += isMenuVisible() ? 1 : 0;
    ignoreClickPreEvents++;
  }, {capture: true});
  dropdown.addEventListener('focus', () => {
    ignoreClickPreVisible += isMenuVisible() ? 1 : 0;
    ignoreClickPreEvents++;
    deferredRefreshAriaActiveItem();
  }, {capture: true});
  dropdown.addEventListener('blur', () => {
    ignoreClickPreVisible = ignoreClickPreEvents = 0;
    deferredRefreshAriaActiveItem(100);
  }, {capture: true});
  dropdown.addEventListener('mouseup', () => {
    setTimeout(() => {
      ignoreClickPreVisible = ignoreClickPreEvents = 0;
      deferredRefreshAriaActiveItem(100);
    }, 0);
  }, {capture: true});
  dropdown.addEventListener('click', (e: MouseEvent) => {
    if (isMenuVisible() &&
      ignoreClickPreVisible !== 2 && // dropdown is switch from invisible to visible
      ignoreClickPreEvents === 2 // the click event is related to mousedown+focus
    ) {
      e.stopPropagation(); // if the dropdown menu has been opened by focus, do not trigger the next click event again
    }
    ignoreClickPreEvents = ignoreClickPreVisible = 0;
  }, {capture: true});
}

---
name: own-words-for-graded-writing
description: "For graded reflective writing (Q&A, check-ins), give facts; they write it lighter themselves; edit only for form and accuracy"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 9365aaa8-2060-49df-89d0-5f0ee4f8a378
  modified: 2026-10-18T06:35:46.586Z
---

For graded writing that is meant to show their own understanding (D6 diagram Q&A, D7 check-in),
offer the facts as bullets, not finished answers. They deliberately write it lighter on detail than
the facts given, so it reflects what they actually understand and can recall. When asked to check
it, fix spelling, formatting and sentence structure, and correct only factual errors, explaining
each one. Keep their voice and level of detail, and don't add points they left out.

**Why:** the user, 2026-10-18 (issue #56 Q&A): "I could copy what you told me, but it does not truly
represent what I understand, and so I kept it a little lighter on details that make it easier for
me to learn and recollect."

**How to apply:** note any factual corrections separately from the wording changes. Related:
[[teach-through-navigation]], [[one-step-at-a-time]].

The user sometimes copies a draft Claude wrote into their own file and edits it there, so their edits
and Claude's never overwrite each other. On issue #56 Claude wrote `.specstory/issue-56-design-decisions.md`
and `issue-56-tech-debt.md`; the user's own copies, the ones they actually paste, were
`.specstory/decisions.md` and `.specstory/tech-debt.md`. They don't always say when they do this.

**Why:** on 2026-10-18 Claude applied review fixes only to its own copies, and the user had to point
out the files that counted ("my personal ones so they do not come in between of your edits").

**How to apply:** before reporting a fix to any draft (decisions, tech debt, PR text, Q&A notes), run
`ls -la .specstory/` and look for user-made files with similar names or content. Apply the fix to the
user's copy too, keeping their wording, and say which files changed. If it's unclear which copy
counts, ask. Treat the user's copy as the one that matters. Plain typos in their copy may be fixed
directly ("can fix typos, idc", 2026-10-18); wording stays theirs. They reuse the same two names per
issue: `.specstory/decisions.md` and `.specstory/tech-debt.md` hold the *current* issue (overwritten
for #58, then #59); Claude writes `issue-<N>-design-decisions.md` / `issue-<N>-tech-debt.md`. "This is
my way of making changes without impacting your stuff" (2026-10-19). Related: [[one-step-at-a-time]],
[[track-real-tech-debt]], [[own-words-for-graded-writing]].
issue-56-pr-description.md
issue-58-pr-description.md
issue-59-pr-description.md

### Code Review — @ab-wm

**Checked:** Read both test files against the code they test (`web_src/js/modules/fomantic/dropdown.ts`, `web_src/js/webcomponents/aria-menu.ts`). Confirmed #104 in the source: the `keyup` refresh only runs for Arrow keys (`dropdown.ts:293`), so nothing updates `aria-expanded` after Escape. Checked in Playwright 1.61.1, and with a small Firefox script, what the `aria-controls` assertions do when the attribute is missing. I did not run the e2e suite. Both CodeRabbit comments are addressed, and the replies explain the changes.

All three points are **optional**. None of them blocks the merge.

1. **Optional: assert that `aria-controls` exists before reading it.** `menus.test.ts:48` and `multiselect-aria.test.ts:66` read it with `getAttribute(...)!`. If a later change drops the attribute, that read returns `null`. Playwright treats `null` as an options object, so the test fails with `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'timeout')` instead of your message that names the trigger. The test still fails, but the PR says "the failure names the attribute." You could add `await expect(trigger).toHaveAttribute('aria-controls', /.+/)` first, as you already do for `aria-activedescendant` at line 70. The `!` rule in `AGENTS.md` is meant for values that always exist, and this test is checking for the case where the value is missing.
2. **Optional, a question: which timer does the 200 ms skip?** The description, the Tech Debt section and the comment at `multiselect-aria.test.ts:92` all say that focusing the picker schedules a refresh 100 ms later. In `dropdown.ts`, though, focus schedules the refresh with no delay (line 308). The 100 ms refreshes come from `blur` (312) and `mouseup` (317). The test works either way. The point is that the Tech Debt note should name the delay the test actually depends on.
3. **Optional: AC5 wording.** "Every new or changed test calls `assertNoJsError`" is not quite true, because the `test.fail()` test cannot reach that call. You explain why in the CodeRabbit reply. One sentence in the description would explain it there too.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-23 01:02:28Z)**_

I'd approve PR #105. The tests check real behaviour, CodeRabbit's two comments were fixed and answered, and I found nothing that should block it. I have three optional points, all small.

1. **`aria-controls` is read with `!` but never checked first** (`menus.test.ts:48`, `multiselect-aria.test.ts:66`). I first suspected this would let a missing attribute pass. I tested that with a small Firefox script, and it doesn't: the test still fails. But Playwright treats the `null` as an options object, so the error says `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'timeout')` instead of naming the trigger. That doesn't match the PR's claim that "the failure names the attribute." The fix is to check the attribute exists before reading it, which they already do for `aria-activedescendant` at line 70.
2. **The timing explanation looks wrong** (a question for them, not a bug). The PR text and the comment at `multiselect-aria.test.ts:92` say focusing schedules a refresh 100 ms later. In `dropdown.ts`, focus schedules it with no delay (line 308); the 100 ms ones come from blur (312) and mouseup (317). The test works either way, but the Tech Debt note should name the delay the test really depends on.
3. **The AC5 claim is slightly overstated.** "Every new or changed test calls `assertNoJsError`" isn't true for the `test.fail()` test, which can never reach that line. Their CodeRabbit reply explains why, and one sentence in the PR description would too.

Bug #104 is real: nothing updates `aria-expanded` after Escape, because only arrow keys trigger a refresh (`dropdown.ts:293`). CodeRabbit's course checks all passed, so there's nothing on the format side to flag.

**What I checked:** I read both test files against `dropdown.ts` and `aria-menu.ts`, and the Playwright 1.61.1 source plus a small script for point 1. I did not run the e2e suite. The author reports 19 passed in Chromium and WebKit. I can run it in a separate worktree if you want the review to say you tested it.
